refutes.claim: The suppress-generation early return now runs after the nested-formatter loop, so a `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` type with a property the generator could not set can now get MsgPack011 (partial type required). On base the early return came before this loop, so this diagnostic was skipped. A suppressed type gets no generated formatter, so it never needs to be partial. The added README text confirms MsgPack011 is now reported for these types. MsgPack011 is an Error (L2), so code that built before could now fail to build. That conflicts with the criterion that suppressed behaviour matches 3.1.0, unless 3.1.0 also reported MsgPack011 for suppressed types. Neither the requirement nor the ledger says whether it did.

title: Receipts/DuplicateKeyReceiptTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (1 tests): no defect shown; refutes 2 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1, logic-edge-2

refutes.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards turn duplicate keys into silent data loss. Take a `[MessagePackObject]` with two members that share an int key, e.g. `[Key(0)] public int A` and `[Key(0)] public int B` (or two members sharing a string key). On base, `Dictionary.Add` threw, so the build failed loudly with AD0001/CS8785. On head the second member is silently dropped from `intMembers`/`stringMembers`, and nothing in the visible code reports a diagnostic in its place. The generated formatter never serializes or deserializes `B`, and the analyzer reports nothing. The dynamic resolver rejects duplicated keys, so source-generated and dynamic behaviour now diverge.

The same unguarded-to-silent change is duplicated in the second member-collection loop (fields/properties path at 1160-1186). Duplicate int or string keys there are also silently discarded with no diagnostic.
